subject: CSEC Mathematics
question: 5 workers complete a job in 10 days. At the same rate, how many days would 10 workers take?
worked_solution: Workers × days is constant: 5×10=50. Thus days=50÷10=5.
hints: More workers means fewer days.
Set up workers × days as a constant.
common_mistakes: Treating this as direct proportion.
Forgetting that the product stays constant.

subject: CSEC Mathematics
question: The time, t, taken to complete a job varies inversely as the number of workers, n. If 6 workers take 15 hours to complete the job, how long will 10 workers take?
stem: The time, t, taken to complete a job varies inversely as the number of workers, n. If 6 workers take 15 hours to complete the job, how long will 10 workers take?

misconception.label: Subtracted rather than using the variation rule
misconception.remediation_hint: Set up t = k/n and find k first.

misconception.label: Used direct variation instead of inverse
misconception.remediation_hint: More workers means LESS time, so the answer must be under 15 hours.

misconception.label: Found the constant k but forgot to divide by 10
misconception.remediation_hint: k = 90 is the constant, not the answer; t = 90/10.

worked_solution: Inverse variation: t = k/n, so k = t x n. k = 15 × 6 = 90. With 10 workers, t = 90 / 10 = 9 hours.
hints: Set up t = k/n and find k first.
More workers means LESS time, so the answer must be under 15 hours.
k = 90 is the constant, not the answer; t = 90/10.
common_mistakes: Subtracted rather than using the variation rule
Used direct variation instead of inverse
Found the constant k but forgot to divide by 10
exam_skill: Use a constant product to solve an inverse variation problem
